questions.stem: What is the fundamental difference in the data used by Supervised Learning and Unsupervised Learning?
options: Supervised Learning uses numeric data; Unsupervised Learning uses text data
Supervised Learning uses labelled data; Unsupervised Learning uses unlabelled data
Supervised Learning uses unlabelled data; Unsupervised Learning uses labelled data
questions.explanation: Supervised Learning uses labelled data, whereas Unsupervised Learning uses unlabelled data.

questions.stem: In Machine Learning, Supervised and Unsupervised Learning are both used for what purpose before complex algorithms come into action?
questions.explanation: Both terms are used for pattern identification before complex algorithms come into action.

questions.stem: Which example illustrates Supervised Learning based on the uniqueness of the data?
options: Animals grouped into those with 2 legs and those with 4 legs
Animals sorted by the colour of their fur
questions.explanation: Supervised Learning is done based on the uniqueness of the data, where for example all animals are tagged separately.

questions.stem: Which example illustrates Unsupervised Learning based on characteristics?
options: Every animal tagged with its species name
Every animal given a unique ID
Every animal labelled by a trainer
Animals clustered into those with 2 legs and those with 4 legs
questions.explanation: Unsupervised Learning is done based on characteristics, creating clusters such as animals with 2 legs and animals with 4 legs.

questions.stem: Which two algorithms are named as the most popular Supervised Learning algorithms in data mining?
questions.explanation: The most popular Supervised Learning algorithms in data mining are the K-Nearest Neighbour and decision tree algorithms.

questions.stem: Which two algorithms are named as the common Unsupervised Learning algorithms in data mining?
options: Logistic regression and support vector machine
questions.explanation: The two common Unsupervised Learning algorithms in data mining are K-means clustering and hierarchical clustering.

questions.stem: Which statement about the output of Supervised and Unsupervised Learning is correct?
options: Both outputs are known in advance
Both outputs are unknown in advance
Supervised Learning output is known; Unsupervised Learning output is unknown
Supervised Learning output is unknown; Unsupervised Learning output is known
Output is irrelevant to the distinction
questions.explanation: Supervised Learning output is known, whereas Unsupervised Learning output is unknown.

questions.stem: For which learning method is training data provided?
questions.explanation: Training data is provided for Supervised Learning; no training data is provided for Unsupervised Learning.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Unsupervised Learning?
options: It creates clusters based on characteristics
It has no training data provided
It relies on decision tree algorithms
questions.explanation: Decision tree is a Supervised Learning algorithm; Unsupervised Learning uses unlabelled data, unknown output, clusters by characteristics and has no training data.

questions.stem: Supervised and Unsupervised Learning are said to have been discussed before under which other topic?
options: Data Ethics and Critical Data Elements
Data Classification, Categorisation and Data Clustering
questions.explanation: The concept was discussed under Data Classification, Categorisation and Data Clustering, and is revisited because it is very important to understanding Machine Learning.
